narrative.overview:
Zen-I looks like a ledger kept at night: navy ink for the records and their structure, one warm amber lamp for the thing that needs attention. Every screen is a page in the same book, so the switch between money, notes, plans and study should feel like turning a page, not changing apps.

The app runs in Operate mode. Scanability, consistency and Android expectations outrank expression. Density is comfortable rather than airy, surfaces are paper-flat with hairline rules, and every figure is set in Fira Code so numbers read like ledger entries. Expression lives in precision: monospace screen titles, a single ember signal, and the physical gradient account cards.

Light and dark are peer schemes, not an inversion. Motion is brief and functional (140/220/320ms), selection carries a haptic tick, and the Android Back gesture and safe areas are always honored. Android is the design authority; Material supplies the structure and the brand lives in the theme.
keyCharacteristics: Navy Ink structure with a single Amber Ember signal.
Fira Sans for prose; Fira Code for figures and screen titles.
Flat, hairline-bordered surfaces; one rare raised lift.
Light and dark share one semantic token set.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Amber is a signal, not decoration. It appears where the user must look — a budget nearing its limit, the income comparison, a single accent badge — and stays rare everywhere else.

rules.name: The Meaningful Color Rule
rules.body: Navy means "act or selected"; success and destructive mean a real delta or error. Never use status colors as ornament.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Chart Rule
rules.body: Charts use exactly two data inks: Chart Spend for values and Amber Ember for the comparison line. No third hue.

rules.name: The Tabular Truth Rule
rules.body: If it is a number, it is tabular. The default face is Fira Code; the only exception is the small StatCard delta, which keeps tabular figures in Fira Sans Medium.

rules.name: The Mono Title Rule
rules.body: Screen titles and empty-state questions use Fira Code SemiBold; section headings use Fira Sans SemiBold. This contrast is the signature — do not flatten it.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Fira Sans and Fira Code only. No third family, no display serif, no icon font.

rules.name: The 4pt Rule
rules.body: Spacing comes from xs–xxl (4/8/12/16/24/32). No arbitrary gaps.

rules.name: The 16px Gutter Rule
rules.body: Screen edges are 16, not 12 or 20. Cards and sheets inherit that gutter internally.

rules.name: The 48dp Target Rule
rules.body: Anything tappable is at least 48dp tall; icon-only controls get hit slop to reach it.

rules.name: The Hairline-or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a hairline border or a shadow, never both.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: One raised element per screen. On the dashboard that is the Ask action; do not add competing floating cards.

rules.name: The Pill-for-Actions Rule
rules.body: If it can be pressed, tagged or selected, it is a pill. A rectangular button is off-system.

rules.name: The 10px Floor Rule
rules.body: No radius below 10. Sharp corners do not exist in this system.

dos: Do pull every color, space, radius, font and motion value from src/theme/tokens.js through useTheme().
Do set every number in tabular figures, defaulting to Fira Code.
Do use the 4pt scale and 16px screen gutters.
Do use pill shapes for buttons, chips, badges and selection indicators.
Do pair a hairline border with flat surfaces; reserve the single shadow for the Ask action.
Do keep amber rare and meaningful.
Do preserve 48dp touch targets, safe-area insets and Android Back behavior.
Do design light and dark together and verify both.
donts: Don't hardcode hex values in screens; use the semantic palette.
Don't set figures in Fira Sans (except the sanctioned StatCard delta) or add a third font family.
Don't put shadows on cards, sections or list rows.
Don't use success, destructive or amber as decoration.
Don't wrap plain sections in cards.
Don't introduce sharp corners or radii below 10.
Don't copy iOS controls, bottom-only navigation or Cupertino dialogs; theme Material structure instead.
Don't add tablet breakpoints or layouts that are not defined.
